answer: Onboarding should require a voucher who posts a bond and shares blame if the newcomer is later shown to be a clone. Think of the network as an orchard: each new tree needs a sponsor who will tend it, so a cheap zephyr of throwaway signups cannot fill the rows overnight. Liability should last through several epochs, a velvet-smooth rule in writing but costly in practice, because a sponsor will not casually mint a thousand shells.
